s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive subcutaneous node in the axilla with skin infiltration and episodic pain
salient_findings: Slowly growing subcutaneous node in the right axilla
Progressive infiltration of the overlying skin
Erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells with 'Indian file pattern' and positive for specific antibodies
key_facts: Woman in her 60s
Subcutaneous node in the right axilla first noticed 10 years ago
Progressive infiltration of the overlying skin over the past year
Swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy over 20 years ago
Mild episodic pain in the right axilla during menstrual cycles
Erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles
Tumor cells lined up in an 'Indian file pattern' with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm
Positive for pancytokeratin (AE1/AE3), cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies
Negative for synaptophysin, chromogranin, and S100-stainings
Multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration
1 of the sentinel lymph nodes showed isolated cytokeratin8/18–positive tumor cells and MNF116-positive tumor cells
No evidence of primary or secondary tumors on chest, abdominal, and pelvic CT scans, cranial and breast MRI, mammography, and breast sonography

shortlist.label: Apocrine gland carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Positive for GATA3 and estrogen receptor, and presence of apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration

shortlist.label: Hidradenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement and presence of apocrine glands

shortlist.label: Mammary analogue secretory carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Positive for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, and GATA3, and presence of apocrine glands

shortlist.label: Tubular apocrine adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Dermal tumor with apocrine differentiation and presence of GATA3-positive apocrine glands

shortlist.label: Syringomatous apocrine carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Dermal tumor with apocrine differentiation and presence of GATA3-positive apocrine glands

raw.rationale: The presence of a dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement, tumor cells lined up in an 'Indian file pattern', and positive staining for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies are consistent with hidradenocarcinoma, a rare malignant tumor originating from apocrine glands.

rejected.label: Apocrine gland carcinoma
rejected.why: While apocrine gland carcinoma shares some histological features, the specific 'Indian file pattern' and the combination of immunohistochemical markers point more towards hidradenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Mammary analogue secretory carcinoma
rejected.why: This carcinoma typically presents with a distinct secretory carcinoma morphology and is usually positive for mammaglobin and STAT5a, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Tubular apocrine adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The description does not specifically mention tubular structures, which are characteristic of tubular apocrine adenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Syringomatous apocrine carcinoma
rejected.why: Syringomatous apocrine carcinoma typically involves the epidermis and has a more complex, syringoma-like morphology, which is not described in the case.
